claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 14 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you tell me: are you responsible for Alex? This would typically mean he lives with you, or you're contributing to the cost of looking after him.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex. He lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now, could you tell me about your own situation – are you aged 16 or over?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. 

A couple more questions about Alex:

Is Alex in full-time education or training, or has he left education/training? And is he currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in any education or training at the moment. And actually, we don't live in the UK - we're living abroad right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I have a couple of follow-up questions based on that:

Regarding your living situation abroad – are you or your partner (if you have one) working for the UK government or the armed forces, or are you otherwise covered by UK social security while living abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're not working for the UK government or armed forces, and we're not covered by UK social security while we're abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I need to share some important findings with you.

According to the eligibility rules for Child Benefit, you normally qualify if:
- You're responsible for a child under 16 (which applies to Alex), **and**
- You live in the UK

Since you've mentioned that you're currently living abroad and you're not working for the UK government, armed forces, or covered by UK social security, this affects your eligibility.

Additionally, you mentioned that Alex is not currently in any education or training. While he's still under 16 so this isn't an issue right now, it's worth noting for when he turns 16 – at that point, he would need to be in approved education or training for you to continue receiving Child Benefit.

Let me now provide you with my formal eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Eligibility Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Summary:

**Alex (age 14):** ❌ Not eligible

**Reason:** While Alex meets several criteria (he's under 16 and you're responsible for him), a core requirement for Child Benefit is that you must live in the UK. Since you're currently living abroad and you don't fall into any of the exceptions (such as working for the UK government, armed forces, or being covered by UK social security), you don't meet the residency requirement.

### What this means for you:

If you return to live in the UK in the future, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at that point, provided he is still under 16 or in approved education/training.

If you have any questions or your circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
